short: English cleric and scholar whose theory of population growth profoundly influenced economics and biology.
full:
Thomas Robert Malthus was an Anglican clergyman who observed the rapid population growth of the early Industrial Revolution with growing alarm. In his highly influential 1798 work, An Essay on the Principle of Population, he argued that human populations invariably grow geometrically, while food production can only increase arithmetically, inevitably leading to a crisis of scarcity.

He posited that this demographic pressure would always be held in check by "positive checks" like famine, disease, and war, or "preventive checks" like delayed marriage, thus condemning the lowest classes to perpetual poverty. His pessimistic economic model fundamentally shaped social policy in the nineteenth century, including the harsh New Poor Law, and directly inspired Charles Darwin's theory of natural selection.
